pr_title: fix: handle namespace import and dynamic import interop consistently
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing! -->

### Description

fix https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/15542
fix https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/15018

### Additional context

From the following repository examples:
https://github.com/XiSenao/exceptional-performance-of-loading-commonjs-modules/blob/main/src/main.js

it can be found that using `namespace imports` to load `CommonJS` modules results in inconsistent development and build behaviors. In most cases, `dynamic import` behaves as expected. That is to say,  it seems effective to rewrite in the following way.
```js
import('${rewrittenUrl}').then(m => m.default && m.default.__esModule ? m.default : ({ ...m.default, default: m.default }))
```
However, when exploring **how the `@rollup/plugin-commonjs` plugin interacts with `rollup`**, it seems that `rollup` will merge the transpiled `ESM` product through
```js
mergeNamespaces({
  __proto__: null,
  default: getDefaultExportFromCjs(rectClamp)
}, [rectClamp])
```
The logic of the `rollup` processing and the rewritten `dynamic import` are somewhat similar, but it can be found that there are still boundary scenarios that will cause inconsistencies between development and build behaviors for `dynamic imports`(e.g. only export `Array` or `String`).

---

issue_context.title: Vite processing UMD package production environment and development environment inconsistent
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

## Problem Description

Condition

```jsx
import * as x from "build"
```

1. the `build` package is umd
2. `build` package has only one default export.
3. Use the above to import

Manifestation

```js
console.log("Mode", import.meta.env.MODE)
console.log("x", x)
```

The console is visible after `pnpm run dev`.

```
Mode development
x ƒ index() {
        console.log("hi");
      }
```

Console visible after `pnpm run dev && pnpm run preview`.

```
Mode production
x
Module {Symbol(Symbol.toStringTag): 'Module', default: ƒ}
```

## Reproduce the project structure description

[Replicate project visible](https://github.com/sedationh/vite-dev-and-production-different)

Note that build uses the file protocol when building the environment.
The build is generated by rollup

![Pasted image 20231117162334](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sedationh/storage/master/PicGo/82b2ccf110fd44f8b419e990c364613b.png)

Note that if you add an export.ts to the

```ts
export const sum = () => {
  console.log("sum")
}

export default function () {
  console.log("hi")
}
```

The dev environment printout becomes

```
Mode development
x {__esModule: true, default: ƒ, sum: ƒ}
```

To debug the dev environment, note that

![Pasted image 20231117162614](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sedationh/storage/master/PicGo/911f8bf1897960a4a86ecc34731857d2.png)

review_comments:
We need to avoid the line breaks here. `toString()` will output
```
(module) => {\n  if (Array.isArray(module) || typeof module === 'string') {\n    return {\n      default: module,\n    }\n  }\n  if (module && module.__esModule) {\n    return module\n  }\n  return { ...module, default: module }\n}
```

Something like:
```js
((m => Array.isArray(m) || typeof m === 'string' ? { default: m } : m?.__esModule ? m : { ...m, default: m })(m.default)
```

@bluwy do you agree it is better to avoid the helper here? I'm not entirely sure, but If `m` is used as above, I think we aren't far from the characters of the interop code of before this PR.

Some of my views, the purpose of using `interopHelper.toString()` is to understand and modify the interaction logic more intuitively. I think there is no need to synchronize the implementation of `rollup` because `rollup` needs to consider the context of the build phase, which is not necessary for `vite`.

We need this function to be a single line because of the way we handle source maps during dev. See https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/c6f0bee7bfc71044121ed5a34981a48ca30a6398/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/importAnalysis.ts#L802C9-L802C9. You can still use `toString()` if the result will be a single expression similar to the new one in my comment

Yeah I think we can keep the function still if we can strip off the new lines. Though I'm not oppose to inlining the monstrosity too. Look at this beauty:

```js
m.default && m.default.__esModule ? m.default : ({ ...(typeof m.default === 'object' && !Array.isArray(m.default) ? m.default : {}), default: m.default })
```

_(I'm only half-serious)_

> @bluwy do you agree it is better to avoid the helper here?

Yeah I think that is a nice middleground too. Maybe a `const interopHelper = (m) => ...`, making sure it's all a single line, and we can inline that instead?

> We need this function to be a single line because of the way we handle source maps during dev. See https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/c6f0bee7bfc71044121ed5a34981a48ca30a6398/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/importAnalysis.ts#L802C9-L802C9. You can still use `toString()` if the result will be a single expression similar to the new one in my comment

Thank you for the answer, I may need to take some time to understand this issue.
Could add a `// prettier-ignore` before it so it doesn't get formatted, but either way works for me
That's great. To be honest, I actually prefer the form of function.

> `typeof m === 'object'`

I am not sure if this just follows rollup build output, but there is a small edge case with this: it ignores a function - there are some libraries that export a function and put properties on it (we have PR in vite-node https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/2435, the library was https://npmjs.com/package/openseadragon). Types for these packages expect these properties to be named exports.
I'm ok with relaxing the spread for functions too 👍 I thought it wasn't possible but looks like JS runs fine with it.

> > `typeof m === 'object'`
> 
> I am not sure if this just follows rollup build output, but there is a small edge case with this: it ignores a function - there are some libraries that export a function and put properties on it (we have PR in vite-node [vitest-dev/vitest#2435](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/2435), the library was https://npmjs.com/package/openseadragon). Types for these packages expect these properties to be named exports.

This fix is aimed at addressing the inconsistency between development and build behavior for `namespace import` and `dynamic import`, which should not affect `named exports`. The behavior of named exports is then rewritten as follows.
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/c6f0bee7bfc71044121ed5a34981a48ca30a6398/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/importAnalysis.ts#L1024-L1030
I think there should be no problem with this approach.

Of course, for `commonjs` modules that only export function, when imported using `namespace import`, the result obtained changes from the original `fn` to `{ default: fn }`. At the same time, according to the resolution method of `rollup`, it will not extend the properties of `fn`.
